takeaway: The cutaneous branches of the radial nerve cross the roof of the anatomical snuffbox; the radial artery lies in its floor.

question.text: Which of these statements about the anatomical snuffbox is correct?

answer.text: The cutaneous branch of the radial nerve lies in the roof of the snuffbox.

lines.text: The anatomical snuffbox is a hollow at the base of the thumb.
The tendons of extensor pollicis brevis and abductor pollicis longus form its radial side.
The roof is crossed by the cutaneous branches of the radial nerve. This is the correct statement.
The radial artery lies in the floor, deep to the tendons, not in the roof.
Tenderness here suggests a scaphoid fracture.
So the answer is the cutaneous branch of the radial nerve in the roof.
